Mayor Ken Sim and the ABC Vancouver party received approximately $1.3 million in contributions from the real estate and development industry during the 2022 municipal election. BC municipalities abolished direct developer donations in 2018, but critics identified contributions flowing through numbered companies, principals acting individually, and industry association networks. The Vancouver Police Department budget reached $382 million — approximately 19% of the total city budget . This is the highest per-capita police spending of any major Canadian city. Despite this extraordinary investment, Vancouver's Downtown Eastside remains the site of Canada's most concentrated drug poisoning death rate. The Broadway Plan, approved by council in 2022, is the largest single upzoning in Vancouver's history — affecting 500 blocks along the Broadway corridor. BC Assessment analysis suggests the rezoning unlocked approximately $25 billion in land value uplift for private landowners and developers. The City of Vancouver Auditor's 2021 procurement audit found that approximately 40% of contracts reviewed had bypassed the competitive bidding process , relying on sole-source justifications or emergency exemptions. Vancouver spends over $100 million annually on housing and homelessness programs. Despite this, the city hosts over 3,000 unsheltered individuals — with numbers persisting despite annual budget growth. The SkyTrain Broadway Extension (VCC-Clark to Arbutus, 5.7 km) cost $2.83 billion — funded jointly by federal, provincial, and transit authority contributions.
